title: Engle-Granger, step by step — and why its critical values differ

explain.prompt: In 5–7 sentences: describe the two steps of Engle-Granger and its null hypothesis; interpret the WTI–Brent result; then explain the coffee–Brent result, where the ADF statistic on the residuals gives a 'naive' p-value of 0.038 but the Engle-Granger p-value is 0.50. Which one is right and why? Finally, what does the brent~coffee ordering show?
rubric: Step 1: OLS of y on a constant and x in levels (the candidate long-run relation). Step 2: unit-root test on the residuals. H0: no cointegration (residuals have a unit root); H1: cointegration (residuals stationary).
WTI ~ Brent: β ≈ 0.98, statistic ≈ −7.4 far below the 5 % Engle-Granger critical value (≈ −3.34), p ≈ 0 → cointegrated: an equilibrium WTI keeps returning to.

Coffee ~ Brent: same statistic (−2.05) but the correct p-value is 0.50 → no cointegration. The naive p-value (0.038) uses Dickey-Fuller tables, which assume the series tested is observed; here β was estimated by OLS to make the residual as small and stationary-looking as possible, so the critical values must be more negative (−3.34 instead of ≈ −1.94).
The naive reading would wrongly 'confirm' a relationship that does not exist — the spurious regression of Case 2 reappearing through the back door.

The result depends on which variable is on the left: brent ~ coffee gives a different statistic (p ≈ 0.20). Engle-Granger finds a single relationship and is sensitive to normalisation, low power and breaks.
Cointegration needs an economic mechanism (arbitrage for WTI–Brent); without one, even a rejection would be suspect.
